pins.title: Sunrise Alarm Clock vs Phone Alarm: Keep Your Phone Off the Nightstand
pins.subtitle: Light first, sound second
pins.description: A phone alarm wakes you with sound in a dark room, and checking it means unlocking a screen full of notifications. A sunrise alarm clock brightens gradually before your wake time, with a sound to follow if you want one, and many models use on-device buttons. A phone alarm costs nothing extra, so here's when the switch makes sense. Not medical advice. #sunrisealarm #wakeuplight #morningroutine #phonefree #digitaldetox

pins.title: Sunrise Alarm Clock Without an App: Button-Based Wake-Up Lights
pins.subtitle: Philips and Lumie vs app-based Hatch
pins.description: Want a wake-up light you can set half-awake without opening an app? Many Philips SmartSleep and Lumie Bodyclock models use on-device controls, while Hatch Restore is set up through its app and offers an optional Hatch+ membership. Features vary by model, so confirm the exact unit can be fully set up without an app. Not medical advice. #sunrisealarmclock #wakeuplight #philips #lumie #hatchrestore #bedroom

pins.title: Who a Sunrise Alarm Clock Isn't For: 5 Reasons to Skip One
pins.subtitle: Light sensitivity, shift work, deep sleepers and more
pins.description: A sunrise alarm clock isn't the right tool for everyone. It may not fit if you're sensitive to light or get migraines, work rotating shifts or sleep during the day, sleep very deeply, already have a bright bedroom in the morning, or deal with ongoing sleep problems. It's an alarm clock, not a treatment. Not medical advice. #sunrisealarm #wakeuplight #sleeptips #shiftwork
